summary: sextant-cli-linux-arm64 ships a Go binary implementing a WebRTC-driven remote PTY
details: The package's sole payload is bin/sxt, a 12MB Linux/arm64 Go binary linked against pion/webrtc/v4, pion/turn/v5, pion/datachannel, coder/websocket, creack/pty, and skip2/go-qrcode. Symbol strings include 'signaling', 'DataChannel', 'pty', 'ptmx', 'command', and 'claude'. This composition — WebRTC data channel with TURN relay, QR-code pairing, and a spawned PTY (ptmx) — is a remote-shell agent: a remote peer can drive commands into an interactive shell on the host running the binary. The package.json license field points at https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control, an unrelated repository whose owner handle ('ddos798') and repo name do not match the declared package identity, indicating attacker-controlled provenance rather than a legitimate terminal-sharing project.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
